approach: Root cause: reading acceptance (`refusing_check`, crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs:520-551) is an ordered list of `step!` checks and none compares the request's explicit parts with the reading's deliverables and criteria. No rule says an explicit part stays in scope unless the request defers it, so a reading that moves part (3) to `out_of_scope` is accepted (jobs 20261029-084645-sza7 and 20261029-110953-bw7k). Fix it at that gate with `check_request_parts`, placed last so every existing refusal keeps its refusing check. Round 5 changes: (1) `request_parts` no longer has its own skip list. A new shared helper `request_own_lines(request)` in terms.rs holds the generated-text filter that `plain_request_prose` already uses (`is_generated_line` with ROOT_CAUSE_ANCHOR and APPROVAL_ANCHOR, fenced code, everything from `## Source` in an approved-work request); `plain_request_prose` calls it and `request_parts` calls it, so the two stay one rule. (2) approved-work requests (`work_decisions::approve_request`, `approve_work`) are a dependent, with corpus cases. (3) Hand-written 'Cause:'/'Priority:' lines are parts text again, because the prefixes are skipped only with the anchor, as terms.rs does. (4) The `Acceptance:` section ends at the first unindented non-blank line that is not a list line; nothing after it is read as a part. (5) A deferral-like phrase in a criterion cancels it for a part only when it is in the same clause as one of the part's distinctive stems (or, for marker words, as the part's marker); a criterion that describes a refusal test in another clause still covers, and a case built from this job's own reading is accepted. Parser: `request_parts` reads `N.`, `N)`, `(N)`, `a)`, `(a)` line parts, inline `(1)..(2)..` sequences and `-`/`*`/`N.` bullets in the Acceptance section (Bullet kind only, never counted twice). Coverage uses distinctive stems so sibling parts cannot cover each other. Enforced by code only; no prompt, config or record is edited.

decisions.choice: 1. Build `request_parts` on the generated-text rules of terms.rs. Factor the line filter of `plain_request_prose` (terms.rs:189-208) into `pub(super) fn request_own_lines(request: &str) -> Vec<&str>`: it sets root_cause = request.contains(ROOT_CAUSE_ANCHOR) and approval = request.contains(APPROVAL_ANCHOR), stops at the line `## Source` when approval, toggles on lines whose trimmed start is a code fence and drops fenced lines, and drops `is_generated_line(line, root_cause, approval)` lines. `plain_request_prose` becomes `request_own_lines(request).into_iter().map(plain_line).join("\n")` with the same output as today. `request_parts` (topics.rs) reads only `request_own_lines`. In an approved-work request it also skips the first line (the proposal title, a summary). Add `RequestPart {marker, kind, text}` (kind = Enumerated or Bullet); leave `request_text_acceptance` and `is_bullet` unchanged.

' lists and must never become parts. `approve_work` (340-345) sends the text through `self.ask`, which runs the gate. One shared helper means a future change to the generated shapes (hestia.rs:1025-1061, work_decisions.rs:299-312) is made once. (2) ..' adds no parts. `request_text_acceptance` is the parse `athena plan` uses (topics.rs:276, plan_entry 411; steward.rs:587/1566/1582/1658, hestia.rs:1781, code_health.rs:1348) and the corpus pins its bullet counts (refusal_corpus.rs:2788-2794), so it stays unchanged.

decisions.choice: 3. Kinds, stated exactly. Parsing runs over `request_own_lines` in order, with a state 'before', 'in section', 'after'. Before the heading: Enumerated parts are line-start `N.`, `N)`, `(N)`, `a)`, `(a)` and inline `(1)..(2)..` / `(a)..(b)..` sequences (start at 1 or a, consecutive, at least 2 markers, every marker followed by text with a significant stem; the last part ends at the first '. ' or line end). A line equal (trimmed, case-insensitive) to `Acceptance:` opens the section. In the section: a line starting `-`, `*` or `N.` is a Bullet only (never also Enumerated, no inline scan); `N)`, `(N)`, `a)`, `(a)` lines are Enumerated; a blank line or an indented line (continuation of the bullet above) stays in the section; the section ENDS at the first non-blank line that starts with no whitespace and is not a list line in one of those forms (a heading such as `Files:`, `Notes:` or `## Notes`, or prose). After the end, nothing is read as a part; a later `Acceptance:` line is not looked for. Parser tests: `request_parts_numbered_line_after_acceptance_is_a_bullet_only` (steward.rs:1579 shape 'Acceptance:' then '1. It parses': one Bullet, no Enumerated) and `request_parts_acceptance_section_ends_at_the_next_heading` ('Acceptance:' with two dash bullets, then 'Files: a.rs' and 'Notes:' with '- keep it short' and '1. mention x': two Bullets and nothing else).
decisions.reason: Finding 4 of round 5, and findings 3 of round 4. The failure class is a dropped enumerated part such as (3); acceptance bullets are the second introspection's proposal. The two kinds need different numbers of matching stems (2 and 1), so each line needs exactly one kind. StewardRequest puts a `Files:` line after its bullets (steward.rs:519-520, 581-585); a copied block or a Notes list after the section must not become required bullets. Reading nothing after the end is the narrowest rule and its limit (a part-like list that follows another section is not enforced) is stated in the doc comment. Many tests run the real gate with short dash-bullet requests (reading.rs:2638, 2753, 2951; drain.rs:3988, 4067, 6320; job_plan.rs:166) and a free-form dash bullet with no heading is not a named part.

decisions.choice: 4. Stems (`part_stems`): strip a leading `[tag]` of a criterion; lowercase ASCII alphanumeric words; drop all-digit words and words under 3 letters. For each word w, let s = w without one trailing `s` when w is longer than 3. Drop the word when w OR s is in `FUNCTION_WORDS` (the, and, for, not, with, without, unless, are, its, can, all, any, one, add, use, new, via, per, but, has, how, out, was, may, our, you, see, two, who, why, too, now), `COMMON_WORDS` (topics.rs:157-161) or `PART_FILLER` (pass, passes, passed, passing, cargo, clippy, fmt, content, behavior). Otherwise keep s cut to 6 chars; then map the stem `doc` to `docume` (`STEM_ALIASES`). `stems_match(a, b)`: equal, or the shorter has 4+ chars and is a prefix of the other; 3-letter stems match exactly only. The unit test `part_stems_worked_examples` asserts: (1) 'Add the --json flag to status' = {json, flag, statu}; (2) 'Document the flag in the guide' = {docume, flag, guide}; (3) 'Cover the flag with a timeout test' = {cover, flag, timeou, test}; criterion '[content] docs/guide.md describes --json' = {docume, guide, descri, json}; and 'A test fails without the change and passes with it' = {test, fail, change}.
decisions.reason: The filler list applies to the bare word and its singular so 'passes' is dropped and the gate words of every generated request add no stems. COMMON_WORDS was written for `topic_words`, which keeps only 4+ letter words (topics.rs:165-177), so 'the', 'and' and 'for' need FUNCTION_WORDS or coverage would be almost free. The alias keeps 'docs/guide.md describes --json' covering '(2) Document the flag in the guide'.

rejected.option: Add only 'passe' to the filler list
rejected.why: Fixes one inflection; 'passed' and 'passing' remain.

rejected.option: Keep 3-letter stems with 3-char prefix matching
rejected.why: 'the' or 'not' would match 'then', 'note'.

rejected.option: Drop the alias and require 4-letter stems
rejected.why: The natural criterion 'docs/guide.md describes --json' would share only 'guide' with part (2) and be falsely refused.

decisions.choice: 5. Coverage uses DISTINCTIVE stems. For each kind (Enumerated, Bullet) with 2+ parts, drop from every part the stems that occur in every part of that kind; if that empties a part, fall back to its full set. Let n be the remaining stem count. A part is covered when (a) one usable criterion, pooled with the stems of every deliverable path whose text the criterion contains, shares at least `need` stems with the part, or (b) one deliverable path alone (split on non-alphanumerics) shares that many, or (c) a usable criterion cites the part's marker (`(N)`, `part N`, `item N`, `(c)`, `part c`; not bare `N)`) and shares at least 1 distinctive stem. need = min(2, n) for Enumerated and min(1, n) for Bullet. `out_of_scope` never covers. A part with n = 0 is skipped.
decisions.reason: Parts of one request share a subject: in the fixture 'flag' is in all three parts, so a criterion for part (2) such as 'the guide documents the flag' would share 'flag' with part (3). With 'flag' dropped, part (3) keeps {cover, timeou, test}, so that criterion cannot cover it. Bullets are reworded more often and nearly every steward, hestia and code_health request ends in an `Acceptance:` section (steward.rs:581-585; replay reads the newest 50 accepted readings, replay.rs:142-157), so bullets need one distinctive stem. The tension is named: a stricter matcher refuses more reworded readings, a looser one misses dropped parts; the replay holds a candidate whose newly refused share exceeds the declared 10% plus the 5-point margin, 15% (replay.rs:296-308). The 10% is an estimate because `records/` is absent.

rejected.option: Assign each criterion to the one part it best matches
rejected.why: More logic and tie rules; dropping stems shared by all parts fixes the stated failure with one rule.

rejected.option: Hand-tune corpus wording until cases pass
rejected.why: Hides the sibling-subject gap; the fixture keeps 'flag' in all three parts on purpose and a unit test pins the stem sets.

rejected.option: Count shared words across the whole reading text
rejected.why: Summary and title echo the request, so a dropped part would look covered.

decisions.choice: 6. Criterion-side negation is scoped to a clause and to the part. `DEFER_PHRASES` (job scope): follow-up job, follow up job, in a follow-up, in a follow up, as a follow-up, as a follow up, separate job, next job, later job, not in this job, deferred to, can wait. `CRITERION_NEGATION` = DEFER_PHRASES plus out of scope, out-of-scope, deferred, postponed, not done, not covered, left out, not part of. `MARKER_NEGATION` = CRITERION_NEGATION plus skipped, omitted, excluded, bare later, defer, skip, follow-up, follow up, followup, for now. `negation_hit(criterion, part) -> Option<&'static str>`: lowercase the criterion and split it into clauses at '. ', '; ', ', ', ': ' and the words ' and ', ' but ', ' while ', ' so '. A clause is relevant to the part when it holds a word whose stem matches one of the part's distinctive stems, or (for MARKER_NEGATION only) it cites the part's marker. In a relevant clause, a CRITERION_NEGATION phrase (any relevant clause) or, in a marker-citing clause, a MARKER_NEGATION phrase makes the criterion unusable for that part, unless the phrase also appears in the part's own text (`has_phrase`, surveys.rs:39). A phrase in a clause that holds none of the part's distinctive stems and does not cite its marker does nothing. A criterion unusable for one part may cover another. `check_request_parts` records, for each uncovered part, every criterion that would have covered it but was unusable, with the phrase, and the error lists them ('criterion "..." was ignored because it holds "deferred"; reword it or cover the part with another criterion').
decisions.reason: Finding 5 of round 5 (and finding 1 of round 4, kept). In this repository criteria often describe refusal behaviour ('moves it to out_of_scope as a follow-up'); the phrase cancels a criterion only where it sits next to the part's own subject, so a criterion about the refusal test of another part, or a second clause about refusal, still covers. 'The timeout test is deferred' still does not cover part (3): its one clause holds 'timeou' and 'test' and 'deferred'. 'Part (3) timeout test will be added later' is cancelled by the marker rule. 'skipped', 'omitted' and 'excluded' are everyday words here (skipped checks, excluded paths), so they cancel only in a clause that cites the part's marker. A phrase the request's own part uses ('(2) Report skipped checks in status') is exempt, so the request's vocabulary never cancels the criterion that echoes it. Bare 'later' stays out of CRITERION_NEGATION so 'Later retries reuse the cache' covers a part it does not cite by marker. The proxy case `request-parts-this-jobs-own-reading-accepted` rebuilds this job's own request and reading, whose criteria 2 and 3 talk about 'as a follow-up' and 'deferred', and pins them accepted: part (1) is covered by criterion 1 (root, cause, descri), part (2) by criterion 2 and the test criteria (test, fail), part (3) by the fmt/clippy/test criterion (test; the filler words add no stems).

rejected.option: Count a phrase anywhere in the criterion (previous plan)
rejected.why: Cancels criteria that only mention refusal in another clause; round 5 finding 5.

decisions.choice: 7. The request defers a part only on a job-scope phrase: its own text, or another sentence of `request_own_lines` outside every part span that holds a `DEFER_PHRASES` phrase and cites the marker as `(N)`, `N)`, `part N`, `item N` (letters: `(c)`, `part c`, `item c`). Bare later, future, for now, separately, defer and out of scope do not defer a part.

Parts such as '(2) Reject future timestamps', '(1) List each file separately' and '(3) Defer the flush until exit' stay required. 'Part 3 can wait for a follow-up job.' is the request deferring. Part spans are blanked before sentences are split. The list is a known limit; the error text gives the repair.

risks.risk: False refusals of good readings that reword a part so it shares too few distinctive stems with any criterion. Stricter matching (needed to stop sibling parts covering each other) refuses more reworded readings; looser matching misses dropped parts.
risks.mitigation: The tension is named in the doc comment. Bullets need one distinctive stem; parts with no stems are skipped; filler and gate words are filtered on the word and its stem; a marker-citing criterion with one distinctive stem covers; one criterion pools with the paths it names; the error names the part, the repair and every ignored criterion, and the reader gets one re-read (reading.rs:738-759). The proxy test over generated-request shapes and the own-reading case guard the common case. The 10% is declared as an estimate; Athena's replay measures it at verification and the planner cannot (no `records/`).

risks.risk: A criterion with a deferral phrase in the same clause as the part's subject for a reason other than deferring the part (for example 'status lists deferred checks' for a part worded 'Report checks that wait') is ignored.
risks.mitigation: Clause scoping: a phrase elsewhere in the criterion does nothing; the phrase is exempt when the part's own text holds it; skipped, omitted and excluded cancel only in a clause that cites the marker; the error lists the ignored criterion and phrase so the re-read can reword it. Known limit stated in the doc comment.

risks.risk: Dropping stems that occur in every part leaves a part with few stems, so a vague criterion covers it, or a part with n=0 is skipped.
risks.mitigation: If the drop empties a part, fall back to its full set; need = min(2, n). Skipping an all-shared part is a known limit in the doc comment; the corpus has a narrowed-part case.

risks.risk: The shared filter changes `plain_request_prose` output by accident, moving defined-terms results.
risks.mitigation: The helper holds the same loop; `plain_request_prose_is_unchanged_by_the_shared_filter` and the defined-terms corpus cases and `approve_request_has_the_generators_shapes` run in `cargo test --locked`.

risks.risk: An existing scripted or stored reading with an `Acceptance:` section or enumerated markers is newly refused, forcing edits outside the listed files (reading.rs:7396, 7743; steward.rs:2585-2639; run/tests.rs; drain.rs).
risks.mitigation: Dash bullets count only inside an Acceptance section. The producer runs `cargo test --locked`, `cargo test -p athena-core steward::tests`, `cargo test -p athena-core run::`, `cargo test -p athena-core work_decisions` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`, repairs the fixture's criteria, never the check, and names the file in the report.

risks.risk: A part-like list after the Acceptance section ends, or a part inside a fence, is not enforced.
risks.mitigation: A stated narrow rule; copied text and fences must not become parts (approved-work and job requests copy whole requests), and the limit is named in the doc comment.

risks.risk: The narrow request-side deferral list misses a real deferral worded another way, so a reading that follows the request is refused.
risks.mitigation: The refusal text says the request itself must defer the part; the re-read can cover it. Known limit in the doc comment.

risks.risk: The recorded request text of jobs sza7 and bw7k is not in the snapshot, so the corpus shapes are rebuilt from the introspections' account.
risks.mitigation: The case `source` strings say 'rebuilt from the introspection's account', not 'verbatim'; the unit tests hold the property for any part (3), not one job.

risks.risk: The producer tunes corpus wording until cases pass and hides a matcher gap, or the own-reading case does not come out Accept as planned.
risks.mitigation: Stem sets are pinned by `part_stems_worked_examples`; if a case's stem count differs from the plan the producer reports it and fixes the rule or the case with the pinned set shown, never lowering a threshold silently.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in reading.rs. Request: 'Do three things:' with '(1) Add the --json flag to status', '(2) Document the flag in the guide', '(3) Cover the flag with a timeout test', once inline and once as separate lines. All three parts name 'flag' on purpose. Base reading from `terms_reading` (reading.rs:7293, wraps `governed_reading` 4635) with deliverables src/status.rs and docs/guide.md and criteria '[behavior] status --json prints json' and '[content] docs/guide.md documents the flag'. (a) part 3 absent: `refuser_for(&reading, request)` (reading.rs:7288) returns `Some("check_request_parts")`; this also shows a criterion for part 2 does not cover part 3 through the shared 'flag'. (b) part 3 only in `out_of_scope` as a follow-up: same. (c) added criterion '[behavior] a test fails when the timeout is missing': `refuser_for` is None and `check_reading_acceptance` is Ok. (d) '(2) Reject future timestamps' dropped: refused. (e) same reading with criterion 'Later retries reject future timestamps': accepted. (f) criterion 'Part (3) is out of scope for this job' added to (a): still refused. (g) 'Part (3) timeout test will be added later': still refused. (h) 'The timeout test is deferred': still refused (one clause holds the part's stems and 'deferred'). (i) request part '(2) Report skipped checks in status' with criterion 'status lists skipped checks': covered. (j) the same part with criterion 'Part (2) skipped checks are omitted': ignored, error names the criterion and 'omitted'. (k) round 5 finding 5: criterion 'a reading that moves the flag to a follow-up job is refused, and the timeout test passes' added to (a): ACCEPTED, because the clause with 'follow-up job' holds no distinctive stem of part (3) ('flag' is dropped) and the clause 'the timeout test passes' holds none of the phrases. (l) criterion 'the timeout test is moved to a follow-up job' with the same part: refused (one clause). `part_stems_worked_examples` asserts the stem sets of decision 4 including {test, fail, change} and the distinctive sets after dropping 'flag'.
